## Problem

Determine whether the supplied string is a palindrome, meaning it has identical forward and reverse readings.

```text
Input:
A string s

Output:
Produce true when s is a palindrome; otherwise produce false.
```

### Example (as reported)

```text
Input:
A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

Output:
true
```

### Example
```text
Input: Never odd, or even.
Output: true
```

The letters read the same in either direction when capitalization, spaces, and punctuation are disregarded.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Ignore all non-alphanumeric characters and convert to lowercase before comparing.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use two pointers starting from the beginning and end of the cleaned string, moving inward while they match.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The main edge case is an empty or single-character string, which is trivially a palindrome.

</details>
